reasons: Lake identity names Thornton v. United States, court U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2004-05-24, year 2004.

The opinion frames and resolves the Belton vehicle-search-incident-to-arrest question for recent occupants.
The holding extends/refines Belton by concluding it governs when the officer first contacts the arrestee after he has left the vehicle.
residual_risks: Role labels are corpus taxonomy judgments, but the disclosed opinion supports SIA Vehicles as the primary doctrinal home.

reasons: The case is not an automobile-exception holding, but the asserted role is only Related (cross-doctrine).

residual_risks: The Automobile Exception page taxonomy itself is not disclosed, so this stands only at the stated cross-doctrine breadth.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the cross-doctrine qualifier wherever this case appears on Automobile Exception.

reasons: The opinion states that Belton governs even when the officer does not make contact until the person arrested has left the vehicle.
The opinion states recent-occupant status may turn on temporal or spatial relationship to the car, not whether the person was inside or outside when contact began.
The lake treatment scope note supports the parenthetical that Gant later cabined the automatic-search rule with a two-justification test.
residual_risks: The Gant parenthetical is treatment/currency-adjacent and is recorded from the lake treatment fields, not independently adjudicated under Lens A.
